title: Triangle Inequality for Geodesic/Path Metrics
description: On a Riemannian manifold, the geodesic distance d(p,q) = inf{length(γ) | γ path from p to q} satisfies the triangle inequality d(p,r) ≤ d(p,q) + d(q,r) because paths can be concatenated and arc lengths add. We formalize this for the intrinsic (path) metric in any metric space.

meta.author: Riemann / classical differential geometry (formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib)

mathlibDependencies.description: Total variation splits at an intermediate point: var[a,b] + var[b,c] = var[a,c]
Reparameterization invariance: arc length is unchanged by monotone reparameterization
Move constant out of infimum: (⨅ x, f x) + c = ⨅ x, (f x + c)

originalContributions: pathLength_trans: arc length is additive under path concatenation (length(γ₁ ∗ γ₂) = length(γ₁) + length(γ₂))
intrinsicDist_triangle: triangle inequality for the path/intrinsic metric
Complete proof using reparameterization invariance of eVariationOn
Application to unit sphere as concrete Riemannian manifold instance

overview.historicalContext:
Bernhard Riemann's 1854 Habilitation lecture 'Über die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen' introduced the concept of a manifold with an infinitesimally defined length element ds² = g_{ij} dx^i dx^j, and defined the distance between two points as the infimum of arc lengths of smooth curves connecting them. This geodesic distance — the intrinsic metric — satisfies the axioms of a metric space, with the triangle inequality following immediately from the concatenability of paths.

The mathematical abstraction of this idea — defining distance via infimum of path lengths on any connected metric space — became the foundation of metric geometry. The intrinsic metric is now the key ingredient in the theory of geodesic spaces (Alexandrov, Gromov, Busemann) and plays a central role in Riemannian geometry, sub-Riemannian geometry, optimal transport, and geometric group theory.

The formalization challenge: Lean 4's Mathlib (v4.26.0) has strong support for general metric spaces and total variation of curves, but lacks full Riemannian manifold formalization. Our approach captures the essential argument — path concatenation + length additivity → triangle inequality — in the general metric space setting using `eVariationOn` (total variation, the coordinate-free analogue of ∫‖γ'‖ dt).
overview.problemStatement:
**Triangle Inequality for Geodesic/Path Metrics**: On a connected metric space X, define the intrinsic (path) metric by:

$$d_{\text{path}}(x, y) = \inf\{\text{length}(\gamma) \mid \gamma : [0,1] \to X \text{ continuous path from } x \text{ to } y\}$$

where $\text{length}(\gamma) = \text{eVariationOn}(\gamma, [0,1])$ is the total variation (arc length).

Then for any $x, y, z \in X$:
$$d_{\text{path}}(x, z) \leq d_{\text{path}}(x, y) + d_{\text{path}}(y, z)$$
overview.proofStrategy:
The triangle inequality follows from two key facts:

**Fact 1: Length Additivity Under Concatenation**
For any paths γ₁ : x → y and γ₂ : y → z, their concatenation γ₁ ∗ γ₂ : x → z satisfies:
  length(γ₁ ∗ γ₂) = length(γ₁) + length(γ₂)

Proof: By `eVariationOn.Icc_add_Icc`, the total variation splits at 1/2. The first half [0,1/2] and second half [1/2,1] are reparameterized versions of γ₁ and γ₂ (via t ↦ 2t and t ↦ 2t-1 respectively). By `eVariationOn.comp_eq_of_monotoneOn` (reparameterization invariance), each half equals the full length of the respective path.

**Fact 2: Infimum Exchange**
For any γ₁, γ₂: d_path(x,z) ≤ length(γ₁.trans γ₂) = length(γ₁) + length(γ₂).
Taking infimum over γ₁ and γ₂ independently:
  d_path(x,z) ≤ d_path(x,y) + d_path(y,z)

This last step uses `ENNReal.iInf_add` and `ENNReal.add_iInf` to exchange infimums over ℝ≥0∞.
keyInsights: The triangle inequality for geodesic distance is a direct consequence of path concatenation — paths from x to y and y to z compose to a path from x to z
Arc length additivity (length(γ₁ ∗ γ₂) = length(γ₁) + length(γ₂)) captures the intuition that concatenated paths travel exactly the sum of their distances
Reparameterization invariance of total variation (`eVariationOn.comp_eq_of_monotoneOn`) is the key technical lemma enabling the split-and-reindex argument
The infimum exchange uses the independence of minimization over γ₁ and γ₂ — equivalent to `ENNReal.iInf_add` and `ENNReal.add_iInf`
The same proof works verbatim for Riemannian manifolds once the Riemannian arc length is identified with total variation for smooth curves
prerequisites: Metric spaces and the standard triangle inequality
Continuous paths in topological spaces (Path type in Mathlib)
Total variation of real-valued functions and curves (eVariationOn)
Extended nonnegative reals ℝ≥0∞ and properties of infimums

conclusion.summary: We proved the triangle inequality for the path (intrinsic/geodesic) metric in any metric space. The main technical result is arc length additivity under path concatenation (pathLength_trans), which uses total variation splitting and reparameterization invariance. The triangle inequality then follows by a clean infimum exchange argument. The proof applies to Riemannian manifolds as a special case, capturing the essential geometry of geodesic distances.
conclusion.implications: This formalization demonstrates the power of abstract metric space arguments: the geodesic triangle inequality holds universally, not just for Riemannian manifolds. It provides the foundation for formalizing Riemannian geometry once Mathlib's support for manifolds with Riemannian metrics matures. The proof pattern (concatenate, apply additivity, exchange infima) generalizes to sub-Riemannian spaces, Finsler manifolds, and other geodesic metric spaces.
openQuestions: Extend to Riemannian manifolds once Mathlib has smooth manifolds with Riemannian metrics
Formalize the Hopf-Rinow theorem: completeness + local path-connectedness implies geodesic completeness
Prove that the intrinsic metric equals the original metric for Riemannian manifolds (completeness of length-minimizing geodesics)
Formalize comparison geometry: Alexandrov spaces where d_path satisfies curvature bounds

sections.title: Part I: Path Length via Total Variation
sections.summary: Define arc length of a continuous path γ : x → y as its total variation eVariationOn γ.extend [0,1]. The constant path (Path.refl) has zero arc length.

sections.title: Part II: Length Additivity Under Concatenation
sections.summary: The key theorem: length(γ₁ ∗ γ₂) = length(γ₁) + length(γ₂). Proof: split [0,1] at 1/2, apply reparameterization invariance to identify each half with the original paths, combine.

sections.title: Part III: The Path (Intrinsic) Metric
sections.summary: Define intrinsicDist x y = inf{length(γ) | γ : Path x y}. Prove it is zero for x = x (using the constant path) and satisfies the triangle inequality via concatenation.

sections.title: Part IV: Application to the Sphere
sections.summary: The path metric on the unit sphere in any inner product space satisfies the triangle inequality — a direct instance of intrinsicDist_triangle. Discussion of what additional Mathlib infrastructure is needed to connect to the full Riemannian picture.
